comments.content: Replacing `null` with `" "` does not restore the intended semantics of "deprecated field is empty": the guard at line 190 is `getSystemPrompt() != null || !getSystemPrompt().trim().isEmpty()`, so any non-null value (including a single space) still enters this branch. Since new entities now default to `" "` and this method re-writes `" "`, the branch is taken on every `createAgent`/`updateAgent`/`mapToAgentConfig` call (i.e. on every `getAllAgents`/`getAgentById`), producing a warning log each time and never actually clearing the field. Conversely, now that the column is nullable, a NULL value loaded from the DB would fall through to `!getSystemPrompt().trim()` and throw an NPE. Fix the predicate with `StringUtils.hasText(entity.getSystemPrompt())` and set the field back to `null`. Note also that the merged `nextPrompt` local variable is never written back to the entity, so the "merge" announced in the log does not take effect.

comments.content: Using a single space as the in-memory default for a deprecated field is a fragile workaround: it only exists to satisfy the NOT NULL constraint of tables created by older versions (`ddl-auto: update` does not drop existing NOT NULL constraints), while on a fresh schema the column is now nullable and `" "` is actually persisted. It also makes any `getSystemPrompt() != null` check (see `AgentServiceImpl.mergePrompts`) always true and leaks a blank prompt into `AgentConfig` responses. Consider extracting a named constant (e.g. `DEPRECATED_PROMPT_PLACEHOLDER`) with a comment explaining why it cannot be `null`, or setting the placeholder at the creation sites (`DynamicAgentScanner.saveDynamicAgent`, `AgentServiceImpl.createAgent`) instead of hiding it in the field initializer.

comments.content: Coordinate-space mismatch: `x`/`y` are produced by `get_element_position` via `Locator.boundingBox()`, which returns **viewport-relative** coordinates — the same space `page.mouse()` consumes. Scrolling the document by `x - viewport.width/2` / `y - viewport.height/2` moves the target up/left by `scrollY`/`scrollX`, so the following `page.mouse().click(x, y)` will land on a different element (and `window.scrollTo` does not scroll inner scroll containers anyway). Either drop the pre-scroll or scroll first and click the adjusted viewport point. Also `page.viewportSize()` may return `null`, which would NPE here before any mouse action.
comments.existing_code:
int scrollX = Math.max(0, x - page.viewportSize().width / 2);
			int scrollY = Math.max(0, y - page.viewportSize().height / 2);

comments.content: Two issues with the debug marker: (1) it is positioned with `position:absolute` but `x`/`y` are viewport coordinates, so once the page is scrolled the dot is drawn at the wrong document offset — use `position:fixed` to match the coordinate space; (2) it is only removed on the happy path, so any exception from `mouse().move/click` leaves the dot in the page and pollutes subsequent screenshots — move the removal into a `finally` block.

Unconditional `https://` prefixing breaks URLs that already carry a non-http scheme (`about:blank`, `file://...`, `data:`, `chrome://`, `blob:`), and because the check is case-sensitive `HTTP://example.com` becomes `https://HTTP://example.com`. Detect a scheme instead of only http(s), and trim the input. Consider sharing the same helper with `NewTabAction`, which currently navigates without any prefixing, so the two paths stay consistent.

`pressSequentially` with a fixed 100 ms delay is bounded by Playwright's default action timeout (~30 s), so texts longer than ~300 chars will always time out and silently fall through to the `fill` branch — long inputs become slow and non-deterministic. Also note the step comments are misleading: the first block actually types (not "尝试 fill"), and the catch block actually calls `fill(text)` (not "尝试 pressSequentially"). Suggest trying `fill(text)` first and using `pressSequentially` only for short texts that need per-keystroke events (e.g. autocomplete-like inputs), with a much smaller delay.

Directly assigning `el.value` bypasses the native value setter, so React/Vue-style controlled components keep their internal state and usually revert the value — yet a "成功输入" success message is still returned, so the caller is told the input succeeded when nothing was committed. Use the native prototype setter and dispatch `input` + `change`, and log the swallowed `e`/`e2` exceptions so the real failure cause is not lost.
comments.suggestion_code:
elementLocator.evaluate("(el, value) => {"
							+ " const setter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(el instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement ? HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype : HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set;"
							+ " setter.call(el, value);"
							+ " el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));"
							+ " el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));" + " }", text);

comments.content: This import is unused: `WaitForSelectorState`, `ElementHandle` and `java.util.Random` have no remaining references after `typeWithHumanDelay` was removed. Also `Locator` is imported but the code still uses the fully-qualified `com.microsoft.playwright.Locator.PressSequentiallyOptions`; please clean up the imports.

With the sentinel value the update path now succeeds silently (previously `null` either tripped the NOT NULL constraint or a `NPE`), which exposes a real data-loss behaviour: `mergePrompts` only computes the merged prompt into the local variable `nextPrompt` and never writes it back (`entity.setNextStepPrompt(nextPrompt)` is missing), and `updateEntityFromConfig` then overwrites `nextStepPrompt` with `config.getNextStepPrompt()` right after calling this method. So for a legacy row that still has a non-empty `systemPrompt`, the old content is discarded by `entity.setSystemPrompt(" ")` while the WARN log claims it was merged. Please persist the merged value into `nextStepPrompt` before clearing `systemPrompt` (and make sure the caller does not overwrite it), otherwise legacy prompt content is lost without any way to recover it.

Actually with OSIV, transaction is per repository call; dirty checking occurs at transaction commit, not at request end. After repository.findAll() transaction commits, the entity becomes... it was loaded within transaction; after commit it remains managed in the OSIV session but no further flush. Before this change the click worked on such pages; now the tool reports "Failed to click" without ever clicking. Scope the scroll (and viewport lookup) in its own try/catch so it can never block the click.
